mutant.description: FOUR mutants planted in mdpf_name_discovery.py, each aimed at a DIFFERENT criterion of this round, because one mutant proves one assertion and this instance carries several. M4: the normalise() call removed from _boundary_pattern() -- the REAL defect this build found in itself, which had already passed a presence-style test once. The module was restored from a byte copy after each mutant.
mutant.expected: M1 -> the ND-TO3-AC1 length-4 assertion FAILS. M2 -> the ND-TO2-AC1 both-arms control FAILS. M3 -> the in-code ND-c-3 assertion RAISES. M4 -> the ND-TO1-AC3 discriminator assertion FAILS. Baseline before and after -> 15 of 15 PASS, rc=0.

M1 -> AssertionError '1 != 4 : forms=[bare]' -- and bare is precisely the least-specific value CVO F1 predicted a scalar implementation would silently return, so the mutant reproduced the PREDICTED failure and not merely some failure. M2 -> FAILED (failures=1): the estate-vocabulary baits are caught. M3 -> AssertionError 'ND-c-3 VIOLATION: registry annotation changed the verdict CANDIDATE -> NO-MATCH. A registry miss is not not-Opal.' x3 (failures=3). M4 -> AssertionError "'partner_tax_free_descriptor' not found in [] : discriminator did not fire on 'CA Tax-Free Bond' -- it is INERT". Baseline rc=0 / Ran 15 tests / OK both BEFORE the first mutant and AFTER the last restore, and `git diff --stat` over the module is EMPTY -- so the passing run is the committed bytes, not a mutated or partially-restored tree.
